name: Cork
tagline: Ireland's food capital and gateway to the south coast
summary: Cork is Ireland's lively second city, built on an island in the River Lee and proud of its food. Graze the English Market, ring the Shandon bells, kiss the Blarney Stone, trace the Titanic's last port of call at Cobh, and road-trip west to colourful Kinsale and the wild coast of West Cork.
seasonNote: May to September is mildest; rain is possible any day.
arrival: Cork Airport is 15 minutes from the centre; trains from Dublin take 2.5 hours.
gettingAround: Walk the centre; trains to Cobh, buses to Blarney and Kinsale, or rent a car for West Cork.
cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work almost everywhere. Tipping 10 percent in restaurants is usual; not in pubs.
foodTip: Clonakilty black pudding, drisheen, crubeens and Murphy's stout.
buyTip: Artisan cheese and smoked fish from the English Market.
